About this policy

This policy explains how we handle the personal data of the people who use this website and our services: visitors, people who send us an enquiry, candidates, students who apply to our university programme, and the contacts of our client companies. It follows the EU General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679, “GDPR”), the Italian Personal Data Protection Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003, as amended by Legislative Decree 101/2018) and the Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 on the protection of personal data and the guarantee of digital rights (LOPDGDD).

Sentences marked Placeholder stand for facts that are still being confirmed. They will be replaced before this policy is final.

Who is responsible for your data

The controller of your personal data is the company that runs this website and provides the Tribyou services. Its registered name, registered office, VAT number and contact details are given in the Contact section at the end of this page.

Placeholder: whether we have appointed a data protection officer (DPO), and how to contact them, is still to be confirmed. Until then, write to us using the details in the Contact section.

What data we collect and why

We collect only the data we need for each purpose. Please do not send us data we have not asked for, in particular data about your health, religious or political beliefs, ethnic origin or trade union membership. A CV does not need a photo, a date of birth or your family status.

Enquiries

When you send us an enquiry through a contact form, we receive your name, email address and message and, depending on the form, your phone number, your company and role, the service you are interested in and any brief you attach. We also record the language and the page from which you sent the form.

We use this data to reply to you and to discuss the service you asked about. The legal basis is the steps you ask us to take before entering into a contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) or, for general questions, our legitimate interest in answering the people who contact us (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Job applications and CVs

When you apply for a job or send us your CV, we receive your name, email address, phone number, discipline, availability, message and CV, and the job you applied for.

We use this data to assess your profile for that job, or for other roles in your field if you sent your CV without applying for a specific job, and to contact you about it. The legal basis is the steps you ask us to take before entering into a contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR). We consider only information related to your professional skills and to the requirements of the role. The people who assess your application decide on it; no decision is made by software alone.

The university programme

When you apply to our university programme, we receive your name, email address, phone number, university, degree, expected graduation date, message and, if you attach it, your CV. We do not ask for a photo, your date of birth, your nationality or your family status, and you share your grades only if you choose to. If you join the programme, we also keep the results of your assessments, your attendance and your certificate of completion. Assessments are scored by people against the same criteria for everyone.

We use this data to select participants and to run the programme. The legal basis is the steps you ask us to take before entering into a contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).

When no programme is open for applications, you can leave your email address to be told when applications open. We use it only for that announcement, on the basis of your consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR), and every message tells you how to unsubscribe.

Sharing your profile with client companies

We never send your CV or profile to a client company without asking you first. Before we present you for a role, we tell you which company it is and ask for your explicit consent; for the university programme, this is a separate consent to share your profile with a named sponsor company. The legal basis is your consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR).

You can withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawing it stops any further sharing, but does not affect what was shared before. The company that receives your profile becomes a separate controller of that data, and its own privacy policy applies.

Visiting the website

To deliver the pages you request and to protect the website and our forms from abuse, our hosting and forms services process technical data, such as your IP address, your browser and the pages you request. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in running a secure website (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). We do not use this data to identify or profile you.

Who receives your data

Your data is seen only by the members of our team who need it for the purposes above. We do not sell personal data. We use these service providers, who act as processors on our behalf under a contract that binds them to protect it:

  • Forms service. Our forms run on Amazon Web Services (AWS), in its London region: an API receives what you send, a database stores your submission and a private file store keeps the files you upload. Files go straight from your browser to the private file store over an encrypted connection and are stored encrypted. Placeholder: who operates the forms service on our behalf is still to be confirmed.
  • Malware scanning. Every file you submit is scanned for malware by AWS GuardDuty. Our staff can open only files found clean. An infected file is deleted automatically, and your submission is marked as having a rejected file.
  • Staff notifications. When you send a form, our team is notified in a messaging tool (Discord). The notification carries only the name of the form and a reference number, never your name, your contact details or the content of your submission.
  • Email. When we write to you or reply to your email, our email service provider processes the messages. Placeholder: the email service provider is still to be confirmed.
  • Website hosting. The website is hosted on GitHub Pages, which processes the technical data of your visit.

Your data may also be received by:

  • client companies, only with your consent, as described above;
  • partner universities, for the data they share with us about their students under their own agreements with us, as separate controllers;
  • our professional advisers, such as lawyers and accountants, under a duty of confidentiality;
  • public authorities, when the law requires it.

International transfers

Our forms service stores your data in the United Kingdom, which the European Commission recognises as providing an adequate level of protection (an adequacy decision under Article 45 GDPR).

Some of our providers, such as the hosting and messaging services, are based in the United States. Placeholder: the safeguard that covers each transfer outside the European Economic Area, such as an adequacy decision or the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses, is still to be confirmed. You can ask us for a copy of it.

How long we keep your data

  • Form submissions and uploaded files: deleted automatically about 60 days after you send them. Files are usually removed within a day or two after that date.
  • Files that are uploaded but never submitted: deleted after one day.
  • Programme announcements list: until you unsubscribe. Placeholder: whether the list is also deleted after a set period is still to be confirmed.
  • Candidates in an active search and programme participants: Placeholder: how long we keep the records needed for an active search or for the programme, including assessments and certificates, is still to be confirmed.
  • Emails: Placeholder: how long we keep email correspondence is still to be confirmed.
  • Technical data of your visit: Placeholder: how long the hosting and forms services keep it is still to be confirmed.

Where the law requires us to keep data for longer, for example for tax and accounting records, we keep it for the period the law sets.

Your rights

You have the right to:

  • access your personal data and receive a copy of it;
  • have inaccurate data corrected and incomplete data completed;
  • have your data erased;
  • restrict how we use your data;
  • receive the data you gave us in a structured, machine-readable format, and have it sent to another controller (portability);
  • object, on grounds relating to your situation, to processing based on our legitimate interests;
  • withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting the processing carried out before.

To exercise your rights, write to us using the details in the Contact section. It is free of charge. We may ask you to confirm your identity, and we reply within one month, which the GDPR allows us to extend by two further months for complex requests; if we do, we tell you why within the first month.

If you think we have not handled your data lawfully, you can lodge a complaint with a data protection authority, in particular the one in the EU country where you live, work or think the infringement took place. In Italy it is the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali; in Spain, the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD). We would be glad if you contacted us first, so we can try to resolve the problem.

Automated decisions

We do not make decisions about you by automated means alone, including profiling, that have legal or similarly significant effects on you (Article 22 GDPR). People read every application and score every assessment.

Cookies and similar technologies

This website uses only the storage it needs to work. If you choose a light or dark theme, your choice is saved in your browser’s local storage so that the website remembers it; it is not sent to us. We use no analytics, advertising or social media cookies, load no content from third parties, and serve our fonts from our own website.

If we decide to use analytics in the future, we will ask for your consent before setting any non-essential cookie and will publish a cookie policy. We do not have one today because there is nothing more to describe.

Security

We protect your data with technical and organisational measures that suit the risk. Connections to the website and the forms service are encrypted, uploaded files are kept in private, encrypted storage and can be downloaded only once they have been scanned, the links our staff use to download them expire after 15 minutes, and the content of your submissions is never written to our logs. Only the people who need your data can access it.

Changes to this policy

We will update this policy when our services or the law change. The date at the top of the page shows when it last changed. If a change affects how we use data you have already given us, we will tell you before it applies.
